# Baseline decisions and artifact operations

This is an application of the current files named in `source-hashes.json`. It does not propose new policy. The temporary directory is a test harness output location, not a replacement production `.ai-delivery` root. No production or device operation was performed.

## Decision and rationale transcript

The following are my actual choices and rationales for this run, preserved verbatim for the baseline evaluator.

> I will not close the slice just because tests are green. The given production mount, stale response, wrong mock contract, old send/fail/quote states, open review finding, and unresolved motion applicability exceed the passing tests' evidence scope.

> I will update RET-001 in place rather than create another weight record. A second repair of the same symptom belongs with its first material attempt. The first repair's original mechanism and evidence remain historical facts; the new report reopens the outcome rather than retroactively erasing them.

> I will keep gradient, row metrics, font selection, parent-only icon border, production mounting, stale-response handling, mock contract, intermittent night failure, product choice, callback leak, initialization race, and static-only loading evidence distinguishable. No supplied evidence proves that all visual symptoms share one root cause, or that the night failure is caused by the initialization race.

> I will put default/send/fail/quote coverage in the production-integration record instead of adding one problem row per state. The coherent failure here is that default component evidence was being used to imply production/state integration. If investigation finds independent mechanisms, I will split the record while retaining links and evidence.

> I will omit the already-fixed one-line label typo because the guidance explicitly excludes spelling and mechanical fixes without a reusable lesson. Its implementation/change record may still show the correction; it does not earn a retrospective entry merely because the user mentioned it.

> I will retain the no-border product choice only in this requirement's ledger and canonical design decision. The current skill explicitly says requirement-only changes remain in the ledger but are not indexed. This is not a generally applicable lesson that borders are wrong.

> I will record the unreplicated night failure with unverified confidence and exclude it from the project index. The current skill permits unconfirmed causes in the ledger but does not authorize a guessed root cause or a successful fix claim.

> I will record the AI-discovered callback leak and review-discovered initialization race. The recording trigger is the substantive failure and reuse value, not which person found it. Whether an unrelated leak should be repaired now is a scope question separate from whether it should be remembered.

> I will not index any reusable fix from this supplied scenario yet. Findings are given, but no concrete repair, exact causal evidence, or completed verification was provided. All reusable rows stay conservative until current evidence establishes the qualification fields. The product choice is confirmed but requirement-only, so it also remains excluded.

> I will not invent the original RET-001 text, failed commands, file names, numerical measurements, root causes, or successful attempts. The existing ledger must be read before applying the delta; this example explicitly marks missing content and pending verification.

## Exact retrospective update operations

1. Read current requirement map and existing RET-001 detail. Read the compact project index, select historical matches by observable trigger plus applicability, and load only those linked sections. Similar words alone do not authorize a historical repair.
2. Preserve RET-001 ID, original heading/anchor, original font-selection evidence, and first material repair. Append second user correction, new diagnostic results, second repair attempt and its reason/outcome, current solution status, changed minimal path, and open boundaries. Update its map row to reflect recurrence and conservative indexing while unresolved. The sample heading is illustrative; do not rename a real existing anchor to match it.
3. Add RET-002 through RET-012 as sample map/detail records. Replace placeholders/pending statements only with actual evidence as work proceeds. Record every substantive wrong attempt before the next approach; do not backfill plausible fictional attempts during closing. Do not erase a failed direction once a later correction succeeds.
4. After actual ledger writes, tell the user the ID, added information, and canonical ledger path. Example notification: “Updated RET-001 with the second weight correction and reopened verification; added RET-002–RET-012 for gradient, row geometry, parent composition, mounting/state coverage, stale responses, mock contract, night failure, changed border choice, callback lifetime, initialization readiness, and motion evidence boundaries. Ledger: `<canonical-req-root>/retrospective.md`.”
5. During final review, inspect the full records and update exactly one parseable reviewed-at marker to that review's ISO-8601 time. Its calendar date must match archive date. Do not create a fresh marker merely to bypass the review. Check legacy map format and upgrade in place if needed without dropping rows. Only after all actual gates pass and CP-ARCHIVE is explicitly confirmed does the archive command update status in place and route qualifying rows to the index. It does not author or audit the ledger.

The actual sample-write notification for this evaluation is: “RET-001 sample adds the second-repair delta without overwriting unavailable original history. RET-002–RET-012 sample captures the remaining substantive findings and decision/evidence boundaries. Sample ledger: `/private/tmp/ai-delivery-eval-baseline/retrospective.md`.”

## What is intentionally omitted

The one-line label typo has no RET row. Mechanical command corrections have no row unless they carry a substantive reusable failure. No made-up first repair details, measured geometry, asset alpha diagnosis, request token implementation, leak stack, initialization trace, exact mock fields, screenshot/GIF path, passing rerun, archive command execution, or fabricated user approval is included.

No full failure narrative is copied into a project routing index. No automatic classification of a requirement-local decision as reusable is performed. No requirement-global blocker is inferred while safe runnable work remains. The sample does not decide any live workflow status on behalf of the parent orchestrator.

## Small governed task

“Small” is not permission to create external framework paperwork, and it does not by itself waive a schema-2 design contract. For an ordinary ungoverned one-line fix, this orchestrator is not triggered solely by task size; follow the host workflow. For a small task already governed by `.ai-delivery`:

1. Read binding/status and reconcile before trusting `todo.md`. Re-audit active legacy status before routing. Keep the same requirement/slice unless scope genuinely requires a new requirement. Use the current checkout by default; do not create a worktree from a framework default.
2. Keep `design.md` concise with the required behavior, scope, acceptance, source relationships, review hash/mode, and solution decision. For existing UI maintenance use `ui_truth_mode=existing` when justified; this bypasses Stage 2 and visual-acceptance artifacts, not ordinary behavior verification. For non-UI use `none`. Ordinary loading/error states alone do not require the deeper state-flow contract.
3. Record selected framework methods once in `decisions.md`, and record current design traceability/hash in `traceability.json`. Use status truth from the actual template rather than regenerate JSON structure from memory. Update verification evidence for the change. Persist `progress.md` only if cross-session recovery is useful; do not add `spec.md`, `plan.md`, or `tasks.md`.
4. If an existing failed attempt or correction has reusable value, update the requirement ledger while evidence is available. Even no-problem closure requires a ledger and actual final-review marker. A trivial spelling fix does not acquire a retrospective lesson simply to fill a template.
5. Supply a canonical output map before any external framework persistence; skip incompatible persistence and write equivalent canonical content directly. Audit Git/content fingerprints and every external default output root at coherent batch entry/exit and before a gate, including ignored files, types, symlinks and SHA-256. Do not create a framework document elsewhere and move it later.

## Complex UI work

1. Audit capabilities and mode. For `figma`/`runtime-baseline`, Stage 2 requires explicit CP-UI, approved workspace, existing real host-stack components, applicable runtime coverage, official previews with absolute paths, current v3 index/provenance/hashes/scopes, static confirmation, motion decision, and clean independent review. For `existing`, do not invent these artifacts merely to make the task look thorough.
2. Reuse the frozen components and workspace in Stage 4; wire actual API/route/state/mount. Keep one canonical `design.md`; stale-response ownership triggers the full state-flow depth. Record execution order, completed/pending work, blockers, commands/results in `progress.md` when cross-session recovery is useful. Do not make a second execution plan or file-by-file design document.
3. Treat `component-only` as excluding host visual acceptance. A parent-only border still requires honest diagnosis; do not manufacture a synthetic host or silently upgrade the scope. Host-scoped evidence needs a production binding. Default-only tests do not cover send/fail/quote; static loading evidence does not prove animation. Obtain current scope-appropriate behavior/visual/motion evidence and required final human UI acceptance before claiming the applicable gate.
4. Keep canonical governance content under the binding's `.ai-delivery` roots. Production source, native tests, official previews/goldens, and runtime assets may use their approved project-native paths. Runtime captures live in the indexed native test evidence root outside `.ai-delivery`; the parent instruction forbids devices in this evaluation, so those are planned operations only.
5. Once all slice gates, fresh clean review, integration and final checks are actually satisfied, the main orchestrator may mark merging/closing truth. At CP-ARCHIVE prepare localized temporary report/index templates preserving placeholders/markers, invoke the archive script as specified, and leave canonical artifacts in place. Do not create archive copies or a `MANIFEST.json`.

## Cross-session handoff and missing old /tmp evidence

Persist recovery-relevant facts in the existing canonical paths, not an additional handoff document: `status.json` for truth; `design.md` and its review hash for current authority; `decisions.md` for selected method and actual decisions; `traceability.json` for source/design binding; `progress.md` when useful for next steps, exact commands/results and blockers; `verification.md`/structured acceptance for actual evidence; `retrospective.md` for failed approaches and minimal future paths.

A useful handoff names the overall composer delivery goal, current phase, completion criteria and next action. Example: “Continue the approved composer delivery. Current phase is integrated verification: finish production mounting and contracted state coverage, resolve the stale-response invariant and review findings, and establish scoped visual/motion acceptance. Start by reconciling canonical status and checking RET-001 plus only matching historical sections; continue authorized work until its gates are satisfied, pausing only for an actual user decision, extra authorization, or external dependency.”

On resume, re-read host rules and current canonical truth, reconcile, read current map, and match historical sections before taking their diagnostic path. Check that reused evidence still exists, matches exact relevant code/input/tool configuration and hashes, and covers the claimed scope. A stage boundary alone does not invalidate otherwise valid evidence or require rerunning it.

If an old `/tmp` preview/log is missing, explicitly mark that evidence unavailable. A remembered filename, old green summary, or newly generated picture cannot recreate the missing bytes or satisfy a bound hash. Recover the exact bytes from an existing legitimate location if possible; otherwise run only the missing scope-appropriate verification in the approved workspace and write new evidence to its required native/canonical location. Update the relevant evidence binding and any required preview-bound acceptance rather than reuse an approval of unseen new bytes. Do not delete old canonical records, fabricate measurements, silently waive motion/host scope, or rerun all valid tests merely because one file is gone. If the lost evidence is necessary for a gate and cannot be restored or regenerated, keep that gate pending and use the narrowest blocker while continuing independent work.

The supplied four references do not define a new `handoff.md`, general backup service, universal retention duration, or mandatory second copy of all runtime artifacts. I will not add those operations as if the current skill required them.

### 1.2 Reusable Constraints

- Match historical applicability and perform its smallest discriminating check before applying its prior correction.
- Keep component, production integration, state coverage, and motion claims within the actual evidence scope.
- Preserve failed attempts before trying the next repair; preserve unknowns as unknowns.

## 2. Problem Records

### RET-001: Second weight repair

**Scenario and impact.** The user reports title weight is still wrong after the first weight repair. The existing record describes font selection; do not create a second record solely because this is a second repair.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Open the reported title context with the existing font-selection path. Expected: the approved title weight. Reported actual: wrong weight. Exact state, font face, and measured values remain to be captured.

**Root cause and evidence.** Preserve the existing confirmed mechanism and first-repair evidence unchanged. The new report does not yet establish whether the same mechanism, a different face/weight, or a parent override causes the recurrence. Evidence now: scenario's second user correction; prior ledger section must be read before changing code.

**AI attempts.** Existing first repair: retain its original rationale, outcome, and evidence verbatim. New finding: its apparent success does not cover this failing context. Second repair: not executed; record any substantive failed second approach and its rationale before a third attempt. Do not label the second repair successful without evidence.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending. Append the actual second-repair delta, diagnostic evidence, outcome, and narrow verification to this same record when available; update the summary row at the same time. The prior first-repair conclusion remains historical, not proof of current closure.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when the recorded font-selection path governs the failing title. First inspect resolved face/weight and overrides in that context. Correct the smallest confirmed selection/override defect. Verify that title plus the prior repaired context. Stop if the font mechanism differs or evidence cannot distinguish the cause.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not repeat the first font substitution solely because the symptom sounds similar. Current root cause, second repair, and final verification remain unknown. Preserve the ID, anchor, original failed attempts, and evidence while extending scope.

### RET-002: Missing gradient

**Scenario and impact.** User reports title gradient missing; static visual fidelity is not complete.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Open the reported title. Expected: approved gradient. Reported actual: no gradient; no captured reproduction supplied.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: implementation defect or evidence boundary, not yet distinguished. Evidence: supplied user correction; no proof of whether source parsing, style application, or render context caused it.

**AI attempts.** No specific gradient attempt supplied. Log the actual approach, plausibility, and outcome before a replacement approach; do not invent an attempt from the suite being green.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending diagnostic check and title-level acceptance.

**Minimal future path.** Applies to a title with an approved gradient. First compare accepted source against resolved paint/style and actual title output. Correct only the confirmed missing application. Verify the same title scenario. Stop if current source does not require a gradient or the source is ambiguous.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not infer that changing weight also fixes gradient. Gradient source and cause remain unverified. Treat paint and typography separately unless evidence proves one mechanism.

### RET-003: Row line box

**Scenario and impact.** User reports wrong row line box; row sizing/alignment acceptance remains open.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Open reported row with the same content and container. Expected: accepted line box. Actual: reported mismatch; numerical bounds unavailable.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: implementation defect or contract mismatch, pending. User report proves a correction is needed in the exercise, not which metric is wrong.

**AI attempts.** No specific fix supplied; do not fabricate a padding or line-height attempt.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending. Capture actual and expected bounds before choosing correction.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when measured row geometry differs from its current contract. Distinguish text metrics from parent constraints. Adjust the confirmed owner only. Verify same content/container bounds. Stop if no authoritative target or reproducible mismatch exists.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not guess a fixed height from a screenshot. Metrics and parent constraints remain unknown. Keep box geometry distinct from font-selection repair until causally linked.

### RET-004: Composition border

**Scenario and impact.** Icon is wrong only in full parent composition; isolated acceptance cannot resolve this host-only symptom.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Render same icon/state alone, then in the production parent. Expected: approved appearance in both. Reported actual: white border only in parent.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: evidence boundary; actual compositing mechanism unconfirmed. Comparative symptom supplied by the scenario. Asset alpha, mask, background, scale, or parent styling have not been distinguished.

**AI attempts.** No specific art repair supplied. Isolated green result is limited evidence, not a successful parent fix.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending parent comparison. Any asset/composition repair requires same-parent verification. Read the frozen evidence scope before claiming a host pass; component-only scope expressly excludes composition.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when the same asset differs only under the actual parent. Compare asset identity/state and resolved parent properties first. Change the confirmed composition or asset cause. Verify in that production parent. Stop if compared assets/states differ or a runnable real host cannot be obtained.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not repaint/export art merely because isolated output is green, and do not construct a synthetic host as production evidence. Cause and production binding remain unverified. Resolve host-scoped symptoms at their real composition boundary.

### RET-005: Production integration

**Scenario and impact.** New composer is not mounted in production. Default tests are green while send/fail/quote remain old. Component correctness has been overstated as integrated completion.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Enter the real composer route and exercise default, send, fail, and quote. Expected: current contracted component/state path. Reported actual: production mount absent and three states still old.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: integration failure/evidence boundary. Missing mount is supplied; precise routing/state-owner defects are not. Test green applies to its actual default harness only.

**AI attempts.** Existing default test: passed in its own scope; failed as evidence of full production completion. No actual wiring repair has been supplied.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending. Wire the existing accepted component through production entry/state owners rather than redrawing it. Verify every contracted state through the appropriate production behavior entry. Use host visual evidence only at the frozen scope.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when accepted component differs from production mounted implementation. Trace real route and state projection first. Correct missing mount/state integration at the existing owner. Verify default/send/fail/quote at the real entry. Stop for a conflicting contract or unavailable real entry rather than substituting an isolated harness.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not repeat only the default test as proof that send/fail/quote are done. Do not merge based on green default coverage. Precise state routing remains unknown; all contracted states need evidence.

### RET-006: Stale response

**Scenario and impact.** Earlier response overwrites newer state; user sees stale results despite green tests.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Start requests A then B. Complete B then A. Expected: B remains authoritative. Reported actual: A overwrites B.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: implementation defect. Out-of-order overwrite is supplied; the actual ownership/guard/cancellation defect is not yet traced.

**AI attempts.** No repair supplied. Existing suite did not discriminate this ordering, so its green result is insufficient for this invariant.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending. This materially changes concurrency/stale-result handling, so audit `state_flow_required=true` and put ownership, transitions, async sequences, and invariants in canonical `design.md` before implementation.

**Minimal future path.** Applies to overlapping operations writing one state owner. First force inverse completion order and inspect accepted operation identity. Correct the missing authority check at that owner using the host's established mechanism. Verify newest-result retention and relevant cancellation/failure ordering. Stop if requests are intentionally independent or product ordering is unclear.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not add delay or redraw the UI to mask the race. Exact cause and implementation remain unverified. Only an operation still authorized for the current state may mutate it.

### RET-007: Wrong mock contract

**Scenario and impact.** Passing test uses the wrong contract; green evidence can validate the wrong behavior.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Compare mock contract with the authoritative agreed API/behavior contract. Expected: same semantics. Reported actual: mismatch, exact fields unspecified.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: verification defect. The scenario identifies a wrong mock contract but supplies no specific mismatch or validated corrected test.

**AI attempts.** Existing mocked test: green for its configured contract; not proof of agreed behavior. No corrected test execution supplied.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending. Correct contract assumptions, demonstrate that the test discriminates the wrong behavior, then verify actual implementation against the authoritative contract.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when mocked green tests conflict with actual contract or reported behavior. Compare authoritative request/response semantics first. Correct the minimal mock/expectation mismatch. Verify the contract boundary and affected behavior. Stop if authoritative contract is missing or ambiguous.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not change implementation to satisfy a known-wrong mock. Exact contract and fresh test result remain unknown. Test expectations need an independent authority.

### RET-008: Night failure

**Scenario and impact.** Night failure is reported but unreplicated; cause and affected breadth remain unknown.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Recover original run identity, inputs, environment, and logs; perform a bounded equivalent rerun. Expected: required behavior. Actual: original failure report; no successful reproduction.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: unclassified runtime/verification failure. Evidence only establishes the report, not a cause. Missing original evidence must be declared, not reconstructed from memory.

**AI attempts.** No attempt details supplied. Any unsuccessful bounded reproduction must be recorded with conditions and outcome; a non-reproduction does not prove a fix.

**Final solution and verification.** None confirmed. Keep unresolved boundary visible; determine acceptance impact from contract and recovered evidence.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when a comparable intermittent failure has source evidence. First compare run environment and signature. Make no speculative correction; change only after reproduction or discriminating evidence. Verify targeted conditions. Stop if original evidence is unavailable or signatures differ.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not label this flaky, assign it to the initialization race, or include it in the index without evidence. Everything beyond the report remains unverified. Preserve uncertainty explicitly.

### RET-009: Product choice

**Scenario and impact.** Requirement-only product choice changes border to no border; this changes the current acceptance target, not a reusable universal border rule.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Compare current canonical design and user decision. Expected now: no border. Earlier target: border. Implementation state not supplied.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: requirement choice change. Evidence: explicit scenario decision. This is not evidence that the icon's parent-only white border shares the same cause or owner.

**AI attempts.** Earlier border implementation, if any, remains historically judged against its then-current contract. Do not invent a failed AI direction solely because the user changed the choice.

**Final solution and verification.** Update the same `design.md` decision/acceptance source and traceability; changed bytes invalidate old review. Record `user_decision_required=true` and bind explicit human review to the exact current design bytes before implementation. Existing stated no-border instruction supplies the choice; it is not automatically review of unseen final bytes. Reassess affected frozen visual evidence if applicable.

**Minimal future path.** Applies only to this requirement and this approved choice. First distinguish product border ownership from artifact halo/compositing. Correct the actual product border at its owner. Verify against the approved no-border target. Stop if the new decision or its affected scope is ambiguous.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not route this as a project-wide rule or conflate it with RET-004. Final review and implementation evidence remain pending. Preserve requirement choices locally.

### RET-010: Callback leak

**Scenario and impact.** AI found migration callback leak; discovery source does not remove learning value or establish a repair.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Register callback, finish/cancel owner, then trigger callback source. Expected: correct teardown/no delivery to dead owner. Reported actual: leak; exact trace unavailable.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: lifecycle implementation defect. Callback lifetime mismatch is a supplied finding; exact registration/cleanup owner requires evidence.

**AI attempts.** Discovery supplied; no repair attempt supplied. Record any substantive wrong cleanup approach before replacement.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending owner trace and lifetime reproduction. Keep it within authorized scope or record as follow-up if unrelated; discovery alone does not authorize expanding production work.

**Minimal future path.** Applies to callbacks crossing owner teardown. Trace register/remove ownership first. Repair lifecycle cleanup at the actual owner. Verify completion, cancellation, and teardown callback delivery. Stop if callback lifetime is intentionally global or ownership is unclear.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not add an unrelated global manager or assume the race caused the leak. Root mechanism and repair remain unverified. Lifetime authority must be explicit.

### RET-011: Initialization race

**Scenario and impact.** Review found dependency initialization race; clean review/closure is not established even with green tests.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Delay dependency readiness and invoke consumer early. Expected: valid readiness guard/sequence. Reported actual: race; exact effects unspecified.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: architecture/implementation defect pending trace. Review finding is supplied; causal link to night failure is absent.

**AI attempts.** Review correction received; no repair attempt supplied. Do not claim a review-approved fix.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending controlled ordering test and smallest readiness correction at existing owner; obtain a clean independent review round afterwards.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when a consumer can run before dependency readiness. First control startup ordering. Correct the proven readiness/ownership defect. Verify early invocation and normal ready flow. Stop if readiness contract is unclear or failure cannot be reproduced.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not insert arbitrary sleep or merge because other tests passed. Impact and causal path remain unverified. Readiness must be an explicit invariant.

### RET-012: Static motion evidence

**Scenario and impact.** Loading screenshot is static only; it cannot establish motion timing, repetition, stopping, or transition behavior.

**Shortest reproduction; expected/actual.** Read loading's required motion decision and existing evidence. Expected: explicit static/no-motion decision, or motion confirmation/waiver plus required runtime acceptance. Actual: a static screenshot only; requirement's animation applicability not supplied.

**Root cause and evidence.** Category: evidence boundary. Supplied static evidence has no temporal dimension; whether loading is animated must be established from its current contract.

**AI attempts.** Static capture is useful for the frozen frame but insufficient as motion acceptance. No temporal verification supplied.

**Final solution and verification.** Pending applicability check. If static, record explicit confirmed static/no-motion. If animated and host can deterministically capture, provide GIF path/hash and motion confirmation; otherwise record reason, confirmation/waiver, and Stage 4 runtime verification. Static visual approval never silently substitutes.

**Minimal future path.** Applies when loading has applicable animation or its decision is missing. Inspect current motion contract first. Supply the missing scope-appropriate decision/evidence. Verify actual start/run/stop/transition behavior at required acceptance scope. Stop if expected motion is ambiguous or the real host cannot support the required claim.

**Do not retry; boundaries; constraint.** Do not rerun the same static screenshot as temporal proof or add a second encoder/format without need. Motion applicability and confirmation remain unknown. A static golden proves only its frame.
